area.title: Transporter selection and adding a transporter
area.scope: The transporter page (list, search, type, status, view details, choosing one) and adding a transporter: choosing commercial or private, the commercial and private transporter forms, their validation, and the new transporter becoming selectable. Stops at arrival details and at the address book's own transporter tab.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

sources.role: the owner's decisions, as narrowed by ruling:sam-2026-10-09: on look and feel the prototype wins by default over what the real services do today; only a DR1 judgement on the same difference, or a real constraint the prototype cannot express (persistence, validation, authentication, cross-service behaviour), overrides it. The prototype never decides architecture.

claims.statement: Wherever a real service differs from Design Release 2.1 of the GB notification service prototype, the real service changes to match Design Release 2.1.
claims.quote: Goal: wherever the real services differ from Design Release 2.1, they change to match it.
claims.note: New: answers no earlier report question.

claims.statement: Which repos change (frontends, backends and other repos) is worked out from the evidence, not fixed in advance.
claims.quote: Work out from the evidence which frontends, backends and other repos that touches.
claims.note: New. The 'not fixed in advance' reading follows from 'work out from the evidence'.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements.
claims.quote: The DR1 parity backlog. [...] It is not a source of requirements.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Nothing is built because the DR1 parity backlog says so on its own; this follows from the backlog not being a source of requirements and being usable only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-07.md lines 7-8 (DR1 paragraph); claim 3 second sentence
claims.quote: It is not a source of requirements. Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New. The main session's claim 3 states this in so many words; the quote implies it.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is used only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.quote: Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Where DR1 already made a judgement on that same difference between the real frontend and the prototype, the DR1 judgement is followed.
claims.quote: if DR1 already made a judgement on that difference, follow it and cite the row.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Where a DR1 judgement is followed, the DR1 parity backlog row it comes from is cited.
claims.quote: follow it and cite the row.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today.
claims.quote: Precedence: the prototype wins by default.
claims.note: New. 'Over what the real services do today' is the main session's framing; it follows from the Goal paragraph.

claims.statement: A DR1 judgement on the same difference overrides the prototype default.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. 'On the same difference' comes from the DR1 paragraph (lines 8-9).

claims.statement: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default; the ruling names persistence, validation, authentication and cross-service behaviour as such constraints.
claims.quote: a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. The quote says 'auth'; claim 6 reads it as authentication. Claim 6 adds 'such as', making the list examples; the quote's parenthesis can be read either as examples or as the full list.

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: DR1 judgements only. Never a source of requirements on its own. Used only where the real frontend and the prototype clash: where DR1 already judged that same difference, the judgement wins and its row is cited.

claims.statement: The transporter list page sits at /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/transporters, and a trader reaches it from the transit countries page's Save and continue.
claims.quote: http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-AGR42S/transporters

claims.ref: trace 94ca6 action call@405 (overview snapshot, section 3. Transport and arrival)
claims.quote: Transport details

claims.statement: On a new draft the Transport details task shows the status To do, in a blue tag.
claims.quote: To do

claims.statement: The transporter list page heading is Transporter details, under the caption Transport and arrival.
claims.quote:
Transport and arrival

Transporter details

claims.statement: The transporter list page explains who the transporter is.
claims.quote: This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment.

claims.statement: The transporter list page tells the trader when a transporter must hold a valid UK transporter authorisation, as three bullet conditions.
claims.quote: Your transporter must hold a valid transporter authorisation, issued by DAERA or APHA in the UK if they are: transporting any live vertebrate animals in, to, from or through Great Britain (GB) | travelling on journeys of over 65 km | transporting as part of an economic (commercial) activity

claims.statement: The transporter list page links to GOV.UK guidance on transporting animals for an economic activity, which opens in a new tab.
claims.quote: Find out how to transport animals in connection with an economic activity (opens in a new tab)

claims.statement: The transporter list page says that DAERA documents are valid in GB and that EU member state documents are not.
claims.quote: Documents issued by DAERA are valid for use in GB. Documents issued in any EU member state are not valid for use in GB.

claims.statement: The transporter list page has an optional free-text Search field labelled Search, with the hint Name, address or approval number.
claims.quote: Name, address or approval number

claims.statement: A secondary Search button submits the same form with action=search, so the search runs on the server and not as client-side filtering.
claims.quote: <BUTTON type="submit" value="search" name="action" class="govuk-button govuk-button--secondary" data-module="govuk-button">Search</BUTTON>
claims.note: No trace in this part types a search term, so what the search matches and how results or no results render is not shown.

claims.statement: The transporter choice is a fieldset with the legend Select a transporter, laid out as a table with the columns Name, Address, Approval number, Type and Status, and a visually hidden Select column for the radios.
claims.quote: Select a transporter | Select | Name | Address | Approval number | Type | Status

claims.ref: trace 94ca6 action call@471; trace effbe action call@1426

claims.statement: A trader can submit a notification using a hand-added commercial transporter. From transit countries they go: Add a transporter, Commercial, fill the form, the overview, the contact address, Review and submit, Continue, the declaration, Continue, and land on Import notification submitted.
claims.quote: Import notification submitted

claims.statement: The review page's Transport and arrival section shows a Transport details summary card with a Change link back to the transporter list (?change=1).
claims.quote: Change transport details (Transport details)

claims.statement: For a hand-added commercial transporter the review card shows Name, Address (lines, town and postcode on separate lines), Country, Approval number and Type.

claims.statement: The review card does not show the transporter's email address or phone number, although the commercial form collects both.

claims.quote: <DT class="govuk-summary-list__key">Type</DT> <DD class="govuk-summary-list__value">Commercial</DD>
claims.note: Inferred from the card's five rows. Whether the contact details are stored and sent onward is not visible.

claims.statement: The submission confirmation is a GOV.UK confirmation panel headed Import notification submitted, showing the reference number.
claims.quote:
Import notification submitted

GBN-AG-26-904TK1

claims.statement: The confirmation page has a Transporting the consignment section telling the trader to tell the transporter that the consignment must go directly to the place of destination, and saying the animals may need inspection and must then stay for the certificate's time or 48 hours.
claims.quote: Transporting the consignment | Tell the transporter that this consignment must go directly to the place of destination on entry to Great Britain. | The animals or consignment may need to be inspected. | If so, the animals must stay at the place of destination for either: the time stated on the health certificate | 48 hours if no time is specified

claims.statement: Every transporter page talks only to the animals frontend, with form posts and redirects. No call to a backend, reference-data or transporter-register service is visible from the browser, so where the list and register rows come from is not shown.
claims.quote: GET http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-AGR42S/transporters 200
claims.note: The source of the transporter register (the approved commercial list and the private rows) needs another source: the frontend or backend repo.

claims.statement: No trace enters a term in the transporter list's Search field, so the search's matching, results and no-results states are not shown.
No trace presses Save and continue on the transporter list with no transporter selected, so whether a selection is mandatory, and its error message, are not shown.
No trace submits the transporter type page with no type chosen, so its validation message is not shown.
No trace partly fills the commercial transporter form, so its field-level validation messages (authorisation number, name, address, email, phone) are not shown.
No trace submits the selection page with nothing chosen, so its validation message is not shown.
No trace checks the format of the email address, phone number or authorisation number (for example an invalid email), so any format rules are not shown.
No trace presses the list's Save and return to overview button or Cancel and return to overview link, so their behaviour is not shown.
No trace shows the review card for a private transporter or for one picked from the list or register, so how those render on review and submission is not shown.
No trace follows the review card's Change link (?change=1), so where saving returns to after a change is not shown.
No trace shows whether picking an existing row from the list affects a saved hand-added record, or how a list pick and a type answer interact.

Hand-added transporters are not scoped to the notification they were added on: a transporter keyed in on one notification later appears on the transporter list of a different, new notification, above the seeded rows, newest first. The list therefore grows with every hand-added transporter.
claims.ref: trace effbe action call@1424 (list on fresh notification GBN-AG-26-PY5SMF); compare trace 94ca6 call@545 and trace d4e42 call@691 where the rows were added
claims.quote: Select Jean Dupont ... Select Lough Neagh Livestock Haulage Ltd ... Select García Livestock Transport SL ... Select Finnish Livestock Oy
claims.note: Inferred because the rows came from other tests on the same stack run: the trace does not show whether the list is per organisation, per user or global. effbe's García radio is id transporter-3 because two hand-added rows precede it.
